cells.B: I recently moved from another country. How can I obtain a Florida driver license or ID card?
cells.C: Are you classified as an Immigrant or Non-Immigrant?
cells.D: Immigrant: Bring acceptable primary ID proving immigrant status (e.g., Form I-551 or I-551 stamp), proof of Social Security Number (if issued), and two proofs of Florida residential address. Testing requirements depend on the credential being issued and prior licensing history.
cells.E: Primary ID per FLHSMV Immigrant list (e.g., I-551 or I-551 stamp); SSN proof (if issued); 2 proofs of Florida residential address

cells.D: Non-Immigrant: Bring acceptable primary ID proving non-immigrant classification (e.g., unexpired I-94 with required supporting documents or EAD I-766/I-688B), proof of Social Security Number (if issued), and two proofs of Florida residential address. Limited-term credentials expire based on legal presence documents.
cells.E: Primary ID per FLHSMV Non-Immigrant list (e.g., I-94 with required attachments or EAD I-766/I-688B); SSN proof (if issued); 2 proofs of Florida residential address

cells.B: I have a driver license from another country. Do I still need to take Florida tests?
cells.C: Yes (I have a valid foreign driver license in my possession)
cells.D: A foreign driver license does not waive Florida testing for a Florida license. Most applicants must pass the vision test, Class E General Knowledge exam, and driving skills test. TLSAE (Drug & Alcohol course) is required for applicants age 18+ who have never held—or do not have in their possession—a driver license from any state/country/jurisdiction.

If the customer currently holds a valid U.S. driver license (another state/territory) and it can be verified, they may transfer to Florida without testing. If the customer does not hold a valid U.S. license, they must meet Florida issuance requirements (including required exams and TLSAE if applicable).

cells.B: I’m visiting from another country for a short time. Can I get a Florida driver license or ID card?
cells.C: Yes (I have lawful presence AND Florida residency/address documents)
cells.D: Florida driver licenses/ID cards require proof of lawful presence and Florida residential address. If the customer cannot establish Florida residency/address, they are generally not eligible for a Florida credential and should use their home-country license (and an International Driving Permit if applicable) while visiting.

cells.C: No (cannot prove lawful presence and/or Florida residential address)
cells.D: Not eligible to issue. Customer must provide proof of legal presence and required Florida residential address documentation before a Florida credential can be issued.

cells.B: I am a Canadian citizen. Can I get a Florida driver license or ID card?
cells.D: Canadian citizens must present an original valid Canadian passport as primary ID. If a Canadian passport is not presented, a USCIS document establishing legal presence is also required. Customers must also meet REAL ID document requirements (SSN proof if issued and Florida residential address documents). Testing requirements follow standard Florida issuance rules for the credential requested.
cells.E: Valid Canadian passport; SSN proof (if issued); 2 proofs of Florida residential address; additional USCIS legal presence document if passport not presented

cells.D: Not eligible to issue if customer cannot provide required REAL ID documents and proof of legal presence appropriate to their classification. Provide the correct FLHSMV document list and advise return with originals/certified copies.

cells.B: I have a commercial driver license from another country. Can I obtain a Florida CDL?
cells.D: Foreign CDLs are not reciprocated for issuing a Florida CDL. To obtain a Florida CDL/CLP, the customer must meet Florida’s commercial requirements, including proof of lawful presence, SSN (if issued/required), and Florida residency/domicile documentation, and must complete required CDL knowledge and skills testing (per FLHSMV).

Non-citizens may be eligible for a Florida CDL/CLP if they can prove lawful presence and meet Florida commercial residency/domicile and federal requirements. Some endorsements (e.g., HazMat) have additional eligibility restrictions. If uncertain, refer to the FLHSMV commercial credentialing guidance.
